answer: An agent economy can throttle sybils with reputation-weighted rate limits: every new identity starts with a tiny quota of economic actions, like a single violet stamp on a fresh ledger page. The quota only grows when independent peers attest the agent's work over weeks, so one operator spinning up a thousand onyx-black clones moves at the speed of one — each clone must slowly earn its own pigment of trust. The attacker's cost is time: maintaining thousands of idle identities that each crawl upward burns compute and attention, while honest agents compound reputation and outpace the swarm.
